rule_numbering: The brief called this rule v1.7. While this package ran, the parallel round-flow agent wrote contract section 31 as 'Rule change v1.7: countries first, 15 min cap, conquest goal' (contract v2.0). To avoid two different 'rule v1.7', this rule is 'rule v1.8', contract section 32 (contract v2.1), test id R23. The report keeps the file name the brief asked for (docs/domain_v17.json).
summary: Rule v1.8 (contract section 32, test id R23): one single domain in every round type. A stress invariant over 240 bot rounds (5 arenas: square, Croatia, Greece, Italy, Norway; classic and the three v1.1 biome sets; lasso on and off; bot-only and with a human proxy) found 183 new splits under the pre-v1.8 rules, all caused by the player's own closures: a capture whose region touches only the trail (near loops joined by the wall raster), a detached lasso pocket, or contested cells of simultaneous returns; once split, a trail from one piece to the other captured nothing ('it does not close the loop'). Fix: SimConfig.SingleDomain (On by default, Off = pre-v1.8 bit-identical) generalizes the rule v1.6 single domain to every round type; a closure that would leave the domain in pieces (8-connected, then 4-connected so corner-only joints count too) takes the band of its whole trail (InheritanceBandHalfWidth 0.45 u plus the supercover raster, the v1.6 band), so the pieces become one domain; the v1.6 safety net severs what an own or simultaneous action still leaves apart (piece of the return cell kept). Enemy-caused splits keep rule v1.5. After the fix: 0 violations in the same 240 rounds and in the 24-round dotnet matrix.

diagnosis.harness: Assets/Tests/EditMode/Core/SingleDomainStressTests.cs: independent 8- and 4-connectivity oracle (no Core helper) after every tick whose grid changed (only the owners whose cells changed are relabelled); each new split is classified from the tick's events and the grid diff (cells gained apart and their source event, or cells lost and their new owner).
diagnosis.first_full_matrix_pre_v18: 48 rounds (square, Croatia, Greece, 4 sets x 4 combos): 43 new splits (38 detached capture, 3 detached pocket, 2 simultaneous returns).
diagnosis.notes: Every violation was caused by the player's own return. Rule v1.5 already handles every enemy capture, KillInheritance islands were already handled by rule v1.6 in Feu, and no trait creates a split. The designer's second complaint is a consequence: once the domain is in two pieces, a trail between them encloses nothing.

root_causes.what: A near loop of the trail far from home closes a region bounded only by trail cells: the capture (Interior + Rim) touches the domain nowhere (or only at a corner). 143 of the 183 splits.

root_causes.what: A lasso pocket made away from the ordinary closure (the loop is loop-erased from the outline) is captured as an island. 37 splits.

root_causes.where: Assets/Scripts/Core/Sim/EventResolver.cs StepReturns, R18 conflict rule (the 'contested' loop right after the capture computation)
root_causes.what: Cells claimed by two simultaneous returns keep their previous owner, which can cut a returner's gain from its domain. 3 splits.

Once the domain is in two pieces, a trail from one to the other encloses nothing (the gap between the pieces stays open to the outside): no Interior, no Rim, the trail is dropped. The designer's 'it does not close the loop'.

fix.closures: EventResolver.LinkCapture (step a, unchased returns, before AugmentCapture): KeepOnePiece(own + capture, anchor = return cell, 4-connected); one piece: unchanged (one flood). Else the band of the whole trail up to the crossing point (InheritanceBridge.BandCells: cells within InheritanceBandHalfWidth plus the supercover raster), minus own, Void and the R1 rim band, is added when it leaves fewer cells apart (8-connected first, then 4-connected). fix.safety_net: KeepReturnersWhole (rule v1.6) now runs in every round type: a returner whose gain is still apart (contested cells, its own land severed in the same group) keeps the piece of its return cell; the rest becomes neutral (TerritorySevered, Other = -1). Documented fallback when no own line joins the parts.
fix.kill_inheritance: Rule v1.6 unchanged; with SingleDomain On, InheritanceBridge = Off behaves as AnchorOnly; the bridge band also leaves out the R1 rim band (only with SingleDomain On, so Off stays bit-identical).
fix.rim: EventResolver.RimSafe: band cells whose center lies closer to the rim than ArenaMargin minus half a cell diagonal are left out (no trail raster reaches them; R1 keeps them neutral forever). Found by AuditTests.Determinism_RoamingFuzz (R1 assertion) on the first full run.
fix.grid_helper: TerritorySplit.KeepOnePiece gains an optional neighbours parameter (8 default, 4 for the corner-joint test); FloodPiece follows it.
fix.runtime: No change. Band cells are Return cells, so TerritoryField.OnSimEvent starts the return fill wave over them in every biome (AddWave from the return point), and TerritoryField reconciles every Grid.Version change. The Fire inheritance sweep is unchanged.
fix.bots: No change needed: a link happens at a return (the bot is home, no stale plan); the safety net touches only returners; bots read home from the grid (NearestOwned, OwnerAt). R23_ABotKeepsFindingItsWayHomeAfterALink and the section 9 targets (BotTests) pass.

decisions_on_ambiguous_points: Band over a living rival's land: the band is taken over its full width, as a capture (the trail is the only line the player drew; a thinner line through rival land would look broken, which the designer wants to avoid). The rival's pieces are then judged by rule v1.5 (it keeps the piece of its pawn). 'Prefer a line that does not take land from a living rival' is honoured in the sense that a band is added only when the capture alone would leave the domain in pieces.
Which line: the whole trail as driven (not the loop-erased outline), so a lasso pocket, which lies on the trail, is always joined.

Corner-only joints: own closures are linked when the domain plus the capture is not one 4-connected piece, so a closure never leaves a diagonal-only connection. Enemy captures can still leave a corner joint (rule v1.5 judges 8-connectivity): kept, measured, open question.
Fallback: when the band cannot join (contested cells), the v1.6 safety net keeps the piece of the return cell and neutralizes the rest (no Capturer option for these).

Pre-existing pieces (custom SimSetup territories only) are kept until a trail joins them or the safety net judges that player as a returner; R2 discs and the Europe start discs are one piece (checked: 0 start violations).
SingleDomain = Off restores the pre-v1.8 rules exactly (classic: no guarantee; Feu: rule v1.6 with the one-cell footprint closures).
Rule numbered v1.8 / section 32 because section 31 already used 'rule change v1.7'.

determinism: The band depends only on the trail geometry (union of capsules and the supercover raster are independent of how a straight path was subdivided into trail points); the labellings use a fixed scan and neighbour order on pooled stamped buffers. R23 cross-rate tests compare events, times, Return cells (band included), TerritorySevered cells and ranks at 30, 60 and 144 Hz; twin bot rounds give identical StateHash every 15 ticks. SingleDomain is not hashed.
performance: One 4-connected flood of the returner's territory per unchased return (O(territory), pooled buffers, no allocation of grid size); three more floods and one band raster only when a link is considered (329 links in 240 rounds, about 1.4 per round). The 24-round stress test takes about 36 s in the dotnet loop (30 s of it is the rounds themselves).
remaining_and_open_questions: Corner-only joints left by a rival's capture (rule v1.5 judges 8-connectivity): 13 visible occurrences (a corner-joined part of at least 16 cells) in 240 rounds after the fix, against 58 before. If the designer considers a corner joint as 'cut in two', rule v1.5 could judge 4-connectivity (more severances) or fill the corner cell; not done (enemy-caused splits keep v1.5 as decided).
A link through a rival's land takes the band over its full width and can sever the rival's far piece (rule v1.5). The designer may prefer a thinner line there.
Pre-existing pieces in custom setups are not judged until a trail joins them or a return runs the safety net.
The band is long for a long trail (the whole trail becomes land): it rewards a detached closure with more land than the region itself. Intended by the brief ('the trail becomes a band of territory').
